To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
static magnetic fields (0.23-0.28 T), which are comparable to magnetic fields found in the human brain, modulate signaling and cell differentiation in embryonic cells.

SMF (1) modulated the expression of genes involved in the regulation of IL- 6, (2) reduced the level of GM3, (3) increased the expression of TLR4, and (4) induced pre-oligdendrocyte markers in the cells.
SMF modulate the signaling and differentiation of human embryonic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the biological mechanisms by which static magnetic fields modulate cellular signaling and behavior.
the effects of magnetic fields on the human body and the potential for these fields to be used in the clinic for regenerative medicine.
the molecular and cellular effects of SMF, and the results provide new insights into the mechanisms of magnetic field effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SMF modulate the expression of genes and proteins in human embryonic stem cells, which in turn affect the cell’s differentiation potential.
SMF can be considered as a biological stimulus that can alter the behavior of human cells.
SMF can be used to modulate signaling and cellular differentiation in human embryoid bodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of SMF are not restricted to a single molecular biosensor or a single pathway but rather that they are integrated into the cell as a whole.
the effects of SMFs are complex and involve multiple signaling pathways that can be influenced by exposure duration.
SMF provide a stimulus that can be used to identify new signaling pathways that are relevant to human health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnetic fields can be used as a probe to reveal the molecular underpinnings of cell fate determination.
the effects of magnetic fields are not restricted to the activation of radical pairs or membranes but can be translated into changes to the behavior of living systems.
the molecular and tissue-level responses to SMF are highly complex and that SMF can be used as a tool to reveal novel biological relationships.
